sections.h2: Who sends the property tax bill for a Raleigh house?
sections.html:
Wake County does. By local agreement, Wake County Tax Administration bills and collects the tax for Raleigh and the other municipalities in the county, so a Raleigh owner gets one bill that carries both the county and city charges.

The same department appraises real estate and personal property. Its phone line is 919-856-5400 and its email is taxhelp@wake.gov. The county tax bill pages also say Wake has 16 cities and towns, and a municipal rate is folded into each bill. Questions about how Raleigh set its own rate go to the city, not the county.

sections.h2: What rates apply to a Raleigh property tax bill?
sections.html:
Wake County's rate page prints a county rate of .5371 and a Raleigh rate of .3720, for a combined .9091 per $100 of value. Wake's 2026 bill page says county commissioners voted on June 1 to adopt a fiscal year 2027 budget that raises the county rate to 53.71 cents.

The county's own worked example for a house inside Raleigh and outside any fire or special district adds a $20 waste reduction fee. Your bill may add more, depending on where the parcel sits:

  • Residential waste reduction fee, charged per living unit, so a duplex has two.
  • Fire district tax, where the property lies in one.
  • Special district tax, usually a downtown area designated by legislation.
  • Municipal fees such as stormwater or solid waste.
  • A vehicle fee for motor vehicles inside a municipality.

To see the exact charges for your address, use the county's online bill search or call the tax office.

sections.h2: When are Raleigh property taxes due?
sections.html:
Wake County mails annual bills in July, and the bill covers a July 1 to June 30 fiscal period, not a calendar year. State law, G.S. 105-360, makes tax due September 1, payable at face amount through January 5.

After that, interest runs. Wake's real estate page prints 2 percent for January and an added three-fourths of one percent each month after. The county says it takes partial payments in any amount, with no prior approval, as long as the balance is paid in full by January 5. Short-term payment plans are possible, and the county advises calling early because it cannot help once a bill is overdue. Past-due taxes can be collected from paychecks, bank accounts or rent under state law.

sections.h2: What happens to the tax bill if a Raleigh home is sold during the year?
sections.html:
The county explains it by sale date. If you sold between January and June and keep no interest in the property, the July bill should go to the new owner, who is responsible for paying it.

If the sale falls after the July bill and before the January delinquency date, the county mails a statement for the unpaid tax to the new owner, and the seller may disregard the original notice. A tax lien attaches to Wake real estate on January 1 and stays until all the tax is paid. Owners who paid through a mortgage escrow account the year before do not receive a July bill, so look up the account online. Ask the closing attorney how the year's bill will be split and settled, and ask Wake County Tax Administration for the balance.

sections.h2: How can a Raleigh owner challenge an assessment?
sections.html:
The first stop is the Wake County board of equalization and review. State law, G.S. 105-322, has that board meet no earlier than the first Monday in April and no later than the first Monday in May, and in a nonrevaluation year it finishes within about three Mondays of its first meeting.

  • Ask for a hearing in writing or in person before the board adjourns.
  • If a decision notice was mailed fewer than 15 days before adjournment, you have 15 days from the mailing to ask.
  • The board mails its decision within 30 days after adjournment.
  • A further appeal goes to the Property Tax Commission within 30 days after the board mailed notice of its decision, per G.S. 105-290.

Wake County Tax Administration can tell you the current review schedule and how to file.

sections.h2: Is there tax relief for Raleigh owners?
sections.html:
Three state programs reduce bills for qualifying owners: the senior and disabled exclusion, the circuit breaker deferment and the disabled veteran exclusion. Wake County's page lists them for owners who are 65 or older with low income, 100 percent disabled with low income, or a veteran with a total and permanent service-connected disability or an unmarried surviving spouse.

The county says the state deadline was June 1, with late applications accepted for good cause through December 31, 2026 on a case-by-case basis. Not knowing about the program is typically not good cause. The state excludes the greater of $25,000 or half the home's appraised value under G.S. 105-277.1, and the disabled veteran exclusion removes the first $45,000 under G.S. 105-277.1C. Apply with the county assessor and ask about the current filing window.

sections.h2: What must a Raleigh owner report to Wake County?
sections.html:
Wake real estate is permanently listed, so owners do not file an annual listing. The exception is change: as of January 1, owners must report new buildings, additions and removals from the prior year when no building permit was issued, whether the owner or someone else did the work.

Maintenance such as painting, landscaping or replacing an existing structure is not an improvement and does not need to be listed. County appraisers may visit a property to check the record, usually 15 to 30 minutes, and carry county badges. Before you sell, make sure the property card matches the house, because a buyer's appraisal and the county record are read side by side.

sections.h2: How should a Raleigh seller deal with unpaid property tax?
sections.html:
Get the balance in writing from the Wake County tax office and send it to the closing attorney. Unpaid tax is a lien on the house, so it must be cleared for a clean title.

If the bill is behind, a sale can pay it from the seller's proceeds at closing, and payment plans may be possible before January 6. A buyer who pays cash for a Raleigh house as-is can often close quickly, which helps when interest is accruing. Whoever the buyer is, ask for a payoff figure good through the closing date.

faqs.q: Does the City of Raleigh send its own property tax bill?
faqs.a: No. Under a local agreement, Wake County bills and collects Raleigh's property tax along with the county tax, so you receive one bill from Wake County Tax Administration.

faqs.q: When does interest start on unpaid Raleigh property tax?
faqs.a: Interest starts January 6 if the bill is not paid in full by January 5. The county prints 2 percent for January and three-fourths of one percent for each month after.

faqs.q: Can I pay my Raleigh property tax in installments?
faqs.a: Yes. Wake County accepts partial payments in any amount with no prior approval, as long as the full balance is paid by January 5. Payment plans can be set up if you call early.

faqs.q: What rates are printed for Raleigh on the Wake County page?
faqs.a: The county rate page prints .5371 for Wake County and .3720 for Raleigh, a combined .9091 per $100 of value. Fees and district taxes may add to your bill, so check your own account.

faqs.q: Who owes the July bill if I sold my Raleigh house in the spring?
faqs.a: If you sold between January and June and keep no interest, the county says the new owner should receive the July bill and is responsible for paying it. Confirm at closing.
